extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers (readers of Proceedings B; academics who review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for academics writing peer reviews for the journal Proceedings B, emphasizing constructive, balanced, and editor-helpful feedback. Advice covers focus, tone, scope, consistency, consideration of author context, and reviewer training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: "The goal is to help the authors make the paper better" rather than simply listing shortcomings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write reviews with the explicit aim of helping authors improve their manuscript; frame criticisms constructively and offer suggestions for how to address shortcomings rather than just cataloguing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge what the authors did well, regardless of recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin or include positive observations about the paper's merits so authors and editors see what should be preserved; balance criticisms with recognition of strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address big-picture issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate on scientific content and organization rather than minor stylistic edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise major scientific concerns (validity of methods, clarity of argument, soundness of conclusions, overall organization) over small copy-edit or formatting points; flag whether minor issues are blocking or peripheral to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Private comments to editors should align with feedback given to authors; no contradictory messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the public review to authors and confidential comments to editors do not conflict; if you provide a recommendation that seems at odds with the reviewer comments, clarify rationale so editors can interpret your stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider author context
rubrics_metrics.description: Be flexible about presentation issues when reviewing work from early-career researchers or those without institutional English-language support, provided the science is sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate presentation quality with scientific quality—suggest editorial or language support rather than outright rejection for presentation flaws when the research itself is solid; be sensitive to career stage and resource context of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain your reasoning so editors can navigate conflicting reviewer opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support your recommendations and criticisms with specific evidence or examples from the manuscript; clear justification helps editors resolve differences among reviewers and make informed decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor emerging researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include postdocs and graduate students in your review process to develop their skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewing as an opportunity to train junior researchers by involving them in the review (while following journal policies), thereby building reviewer capacity and fostering good reviewing practices in the next generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review as a collegial service
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is a collegial service supporting scientific advancement and author development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a constructive, professional, and supportive mindset: reviews should serve the community by improving work and aiding author development rather than merely policing or criticizing.
